passage.title: The River That Came Back
paras: Twenty years ago, the River Brenn near our town was brown, slow and empty. Fishermen had given up. Then, in 2009, a small group of volunteers began clearing rubbish from its banks every Saturday. They planted willows to hold the soil. They persuaded farms upstream to stop fertiliser running into the water. This spring, a salmon was seen leaping the weir for the first time in living memory. Rivers, it turns out, remember how to be rivers, if we let them.
